decision: Which reading of the input state 'accepted + activated Quote row' should WF-101 implement, given that the research defines activation only by its read-only effect and never defines accepted at all?

researched_text: Accepted + activated Quote row (+ its QuoteDetail lines)
Activating a quote makes it read-only so your version matches the customer's version.
The state will automatically be updated to ACCEPTED when the buyer accepts the quote.

merged_siblings.wf086_quote_authoring: A quote's frozen state is spelled 'published'; its line items are frozen and its total is written.
merged_siblings.wf099_contract_generation: Reads acceptance as the shared hs_status field set to ACCEPTED, and keeps its own acceptance ledger.

candidate_readings.frozen_is_activated: A quote is activated when it is frozen: status published, active or activated, or an activated/is_active flag. Acceptance is a marker on the quote: hs_status ACCEPTED, status accepted, or an accepted/accepted_at/accepted_by field. This maps the researched read-only effect onto WF-086's own published status.
candidate_readings.separate_flag_only: Activation requires a dedicated boolean flag that a separate activation workflow wrote, so a published quote is not activated until that flag is set.
candidate_readings.acceptance_implies_activation: Acceptance alone implies activation, so any accepted quote is convertible with no activation check.

best_reading.instructions: Which reading of the documented input state should this build implement? Judge each against the research text and the vocabulary the already-merged sibling workflows use, and prefer the reading that needs no second writer of another workflow's state.

criteria.frozen_is_activated: Activation maps onto the frozen state WF-086 already stores, and acceptance is a shared marker on the quote
criteria.separate_flag_only: Activation requires a new flag no merged workflow writes yet
criteria.acceptance_implies_activation: Acceptance alone implies activation, dropping the activation check

is_confident.instructions: Does the evidence support a decisive choice between these readings?

criteria.true: One reading is clearly better against the researched text and the merged vocabulary
criteria.false: The readings are close, or the state is under-specified
